awd_titl_txt: Conference: International Workshop on Electronic Structure 2025 (ES25)
awd_abstract_narration:
TECHNICAL and NONTECHNICAL SUMMARY

This award will support the 2025 instance of the Electronic Structure Workshop, which will be held June 8-11, 2025, at the University of Texas at El Paso. This annual workshop was initiated in 1989 to serve as an essential forum for exchanging ideas between beginners and experienced researchers in the field of first-principles simulations of materials. The invited talks and contributed posters presented at the workshop will describe new methods for computing previously inaccessible material properties and will present new approaches towards achieving higher computational efficiency and accuracy. The venue for the Workshop moves around the US to enable more researchers without extensive travel budgets to attend. The workshop will bring together approximately 90 graduate students/postdocs and 30 expert researchers from universities, colleges, national laboratories, and industry.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
The 37th Annual Workshop on Recent Developments in Electronic Structure Theory (ESW25) was successfully held at The University of Texas at El Paso (UTEP) from May 8–11, 2025. The Electronic Structure Workshop series was founded by David M. Ceperley and Richard M. Martin at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989 and has been led by Andrew M. Rappe at the University of Pennsylvania since 2015. A total of 160 participants registered for the workshop, including 111 in-person attendees and 49 virtual participants. The local organizing committee consisted of six faculty members from the Department of Physics at UTEP. Seven members of the National Steering Committee attended the workshop, providing guidance to the organizing committee, including the selection of three poster award recipients.  The workshop began on May 8, 2025, with two tutorial sessions on FLOSIC and DMFT. The scientific program then continued with two full days (5/9/2025-5/10/2025) and a half days (5/11/2025) of presentations, which began with welcoming remarks by UTEP President Heather Wilson, followed by 2 plenary lectures by J. Perdew of Tulane University and Alex Zunger of the University of Colorado Boulder. From a pool of 35 nominations, the National Steering Committee selected 23 invited speakers representing North America, South America, Asia, Africa, and Europe. These speakers presented recent advances in electronic structure methods and their applications. In addition, participants presented 49 research posters. To enhance visibility and stimulate discussion, each poster presenter delivered a 3-minute lightning talk prior to the poster session. On the afternoon of the second day, 4 editors representing Physical Review, AIP, and JPCC participated remotely via Microsoft Teams in an "Editors' Roundtable" session. The session provided attendees with insights into the scientific publication process, editorial perspectives, and opportunities for discussion regarding manuscript preparation, peer review, and publication. NSF participant support funds were used to provide free on-campus housing and two meals per day (breakfast and lunch) for all in-person attendees. This support helped reduce financial barriers to participation and facilitated broad engagement by students, postdoctoral researchers, and other participants.
